paper_of_the_week.title: Earlier strength recovery with partial-thickness versus full-thickness quadriceps tendon graft for anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction in competitive soccer players.
paper_of_the_week.journal: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
paper_of_the_week.clinical_summary: This retrospective cohort study addresses Ligament and return-to-sport rehabilitation. The reported population was: Population not clearly extractable from the abstract. The intervention or exposure was: primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction using either full- or partial-thickness quadriceps tendon grafts were included in this retrospective cohort study The abstract reports a favorable association or treatment effect.
paper_of_the_week.practitioner_takeaway: This paper provides potentially useful evidence in Ligament and return-to-sport rehabilitation, but the findings should be treated as preliminary. The abstract reports a favorable association or treatment effect. It should support rather than replace established clinical reasoning and guidelines.
paper_of_the_week.research_takeaway: Future studies should address the identified reporting and methodological limitations, particularly around effect estimates, precision, confounding, and clinical importance where applicable.
major_cautions: The retrospective design increases the risk of selection bias and incomplete data.
Retrospective data may contain selection bias, missing data, and uncontrolled confounding.
The total analyzed sample size could not be reliably identified.
The abstract does not clearly describe adjustment for confounding variables.
Clinical importance or a minimally important difference is not clearly discussed.

specialist_takeaways.sports_performance: The study is relevant to Strength, Recovery, Return to sport. Sports-performance confidence is high. Transfer to competitive athletes depends on training status, intervention specificity, outcome validity, and similarity to real competition demands.
specialist_takeaways.biomechanics: This study evaluates biomechanical outcomes. Biomechanics confidence is high. Interpret mechanical changes separately from clinical significance; changes in joint angles, forces, or stiffness do not necessarily translate into better performance or lower injury risk.
